A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MIRAGE and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing content can be matched across appendix renumbering and layout changes, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original multi-LLM simulations across eight scripts, evaluator ablations, forced-disclosure experiments, and correlations with human evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports a qualitative observation from an attempted temperature-zero experiment.

M1.justification: The script construction, three simulation phases, auxiliary modules, evaluation methods, and prompt templates remain unchanged. The new appendix documents experimental settings without introducing a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight scripts and retain the same script-type coverage and forced culprit-disclosure scenarios. No additional dataset, domain, or task is evaluated.

E2.justification: The evaluated LLMs and evaluator-model comparators remain unchanged in the corresponding tables. SpyFall and other systems discussed in new Appendix G are related work, not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: New Appendix F reports an attempted temperature-zero repeat, adding a sampling condition to the documented checks. The main five-iteration protocol and evaluator are retained; temperature 0.8 and top_p 1 are newly disclosed settings, not demonstrated changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a brief qualitative temperature-sensitivity check reporting repetition and difficulty maintaining coherent conversation at temperature zero. Existing evaluator ablations, script-type analyses, and forced-disclosure tests are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix F newly states that high costs prevented additional repeated experiments. This clarifies repetition limits without specifying seeds or exact run counts; existing plotted uncertainty displays remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing numerical benchmark results, rankings, and human-evaluation correlations are unchanged. Appendix F adds the qualitative finding of excessive repetition and impaired conversational coherence at temperature zero, without quantified or model-specific outcomes.

T1.justification: Appendix B retains the same TII and CIC definitions and equations. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: MIRAGE, eight scripts, four evaluation methods, and evidence that current LLMs struggle with complex social interactions. The new appendix discussion does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly explains the cost barrier to repetition and argues that averaging eight environments sufficiently demonstrates model capabilities. Appendix G expands the argument that MIRAGE preserves real-world interaction logic. The original limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly specifies temperature 0.8 and top_p 1. Prompts, model-version mappings, and resource links are retained. Its cost text, '600700 USD', is inconsistent with the retained USD 600-700 estimate in Appendix C.

R1.justification: New Appendix G elaborates comparisons with Sotopia, Lyfe Agents, Avalon, and Werewolf, and adds SpyFall with a Kim et al. (2024) citation. This extends the discussion while retaining the existing emphasis on evaluating LLMs through richer narrative interactions.

P1.justification: v2 adds appendices F and G for experimental details and related-work comparisons. Prompts and Human Annotation become appendices H and I, with updated cross-references. The existing main narrative and appendix prose are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Existing tables and figures are redistributed across appendix pages and columns, including Table 6 and Figures 4-8. All 29 tables and eight figures are retained without substantive redesign or changed graphical content.

improvement.justification: The sampling disclosures and explicit discussion of repetition limits improve experimental transparency, while Appendix G clarifies related-work distinctions. These are limited gains: quantitative evidence is unchanged, the temperature-zero observation is unquantified, and the assertion that eight-environment averaging suffices receives no statistical support.
